routes.description: Establish that evaluative and moral concepts arise from factual requirements faced by living, choosing human beings, and that those requirements support objective guidance for flourishing and social conduct.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if it identifies life-relevant facts as the referents and standard of evaluation, explains how those facts guide volitional human action, and derives non-arbitrary principles for individual and interpersonal conduct.

motionBridge.description: Connect the factual requirements of human life to truth-apt standards governing choices, actions, and character.

centralBridges.description: Explain why living organisms' conditional requirements create the factual basis and practical need for evaluative concepts.
Show how a human choice to live makes facts about survival and flourishing action-guiding without treating value as an intrinsic property.
Derive rights and constraints on force from human rational agency and each person's need to act on independent judgment.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Distinguish emotions accompanying evaluation from the cognitive identification of life-supporting or life-destructive facts.
Apply the life-based standard consistently across immortality, psychopath, animal-treatment, and consent cases.

routes.description: Establish that moral utterances express non-truth-apt emotional attitudes and that factual descriptions of life, agency, or flourishing do not themselves supply objective oughtness or binding interpersonal duties.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if it provides a coherent emotivist account of moral language and experience while showing that the proposed life standard cannot non-circularly bridge facts to objective norms or explain its disputed applications.

motionBridge.description: Account for moral claims as emotive expressions while denying that life-related facts constitute objective moral properties or truth conditions.

centralBridges.description: Specify what moral predicates express and require the objectivist alternative to identify the alleged objective oughtness.
Show why a pre-moral choice to live or a factual description of flourishing cannot generate objective normative authority.
Test whether actor-centered life and flourishing can justify rights or condemn advantageous harm without assuming the disputed morality.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain how emotive advocacy, rational inference, and useful rights conventions can function without objective moral truth.
Use immortality, atypical agents, and animal treatment to test the scope and consistency of the life-based account.

sections.title: Moral Meaning, Emotion, and Objective Reference
sections.rationale: This issue defines the motion-level disagreement over whether moral predicates report life-relevant facts or express attitudes without truth conditions, and it fixes what either side must explain about moral language and cognition.

sections.title: Life, Choice, and the Foundation of Value
sections.rationale: This issue covers the proposed dependence of value on living action and the choice to remain alive, together with the challenge that a conditional or pre-moral choice cannot establish objective value.

sections.title: From Life Facts to Oughts and Flourishing
sections.rationale: This issue tests the central inferential bridge from biological and human facts to action-guiding oughts, including whether flourishing clarifies the standard or expands it beyond survival without an objective warrant.

sections.title: Rational Egoism, Rights, and Moral Agency
sections.rationale: This issue addresses whether a life-centered ethic can derive interpersonal rights and constraints on advantageous harm, and whether psychopath and abnormal-agent cases expose circularity or legitimate limits on moral concepts.

sections.title: Animals, Harm, and Practical Boundaries
sections.rationale: This issue examines whether the competing accounts consistently explain concern for suffering, condemnation of gratuitous harm, differences between human and animal status, and permissibility claims about animal use.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-05.proposition: Because only living organisms pursue values to preserve their existence, life is the ultimate factual foundation of value and evaluative concepts.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-06.proposition: For volitional human beings, oughts identify life-supporting actions, while chosen values and virtues organize the rational pursuit of continued life and flourishing.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-07.proposition: Moral objectivity consists in a cognitive relation to life-relevant facts, and evaluative concepts lose their basis when severed from the life conditions that make them necessary.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-01.proposition: Gratuitous animal abuse is immoral because life supplies a standard of value beyond humans, and purposeless destruction manifests contempt for life.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-03.proposition: Life is not intrinsically valuable; a person's choice to remain alive logically precedes evaluation and creates the need for values and action.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-05.proposition: The requirements of human life support universal moral principles, including individual rights, because each person's life is their own and requires action on personal judgment.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-01.proposition: Individual rights recognize the factual human need for freedom to act on rational judgment, while rights violators may forfeit freedom needed to threaten others.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-03.proposition: Emotions register a person's values but are not instruments of knowledge; rational inquiry identifies life as the objective standard of moral value.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-07.proposition: Human life as the standard of value means flourishing through the full exercise of human capacities, not mere biological survival, and is more fundamental than happiness.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-02.proposition: General biological values differ from moral values, which arise within the sphere of human choice; valuing animal life therefore does not entail granting animals human rights.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-01.proposition: Emotivism treats ethical statements as expressions of non-propositional emotion rather than truth-apt reports about either objective facts or a speaker's preferences.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-03.proposition: A materialist moral objectivist must identify what objective oughtness is and explain where it exists or originates if it is not an emotion.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-08.proposition: If immortal volitional people could still care about one another and suffer, ethics would remain applicable despite the complete absence of possible death.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-10.proposition: A survival-based egoistic ethic appears unable to condemn recreational animal torture when the act neither threatens the torturer's survival nor frustrates that person's preferences.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-02.proposition: Appealing to contempt for life assumes the disputed value of life and therefore argues circularly against someone who does not already share that valuation.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-04.proposition: A pre-moral choice to live cannot supply objective normativity, because an objective requirement to remain alive must be independently established or the resulting moral system remains conditional on a nonobjective choice.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-06.proposition: A murderer who values his own life and genuinely benefits from killing an innocent person is a counterexample to grounding moral obligation solely in the actor's life and flourishing.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-08.proposition: Invoking rights to constrain rational egoism presupposes the objective moral properties under dispute and does not explain why an egoist should care about another person's rights.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-04.proposition: Emotivism explains differential concern for animals through emotional resemblance and attachment more naturally than a rational-egoist derivation does.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-09.proposition: Human life or flourishing does not adequately define moral goodness because it omits familiar ethical concern for other people and animals.
